senses.gloss:
itikartavyatā
(‘mode of performing a duty’)
------------------------------------------
This is a technical term used in the Pūrvamīmāṁsā Sutras (11.2.8). It answers the question as to how a thing is to be accomplished.
When someone is hungry, he has to prepare ड़ोओद् and eat it. For this he has to cook the raw rice, for which again, he has to get the necessary vessels and also prepare fire using fuel sticks.
Similarly, if a person wants to perform a Vedic sacrifice, he must be given detailed, step-by-step, instructions. This is called ‘itikartavyatā’.

itihāsa
(‘thus it was’)
------------------------------------------
The Rāmāyaṇa and the Mahābhārata are known as ‘itihāsa’ or epics. An इतिहास narrates a story that happened in the ancient days, and has come down to us by oral tradition. It may later be put in writing.
As per the definition given in some Sanskrit works, an इतिहास must contain topics dealing with all the four पुरुषार्थस् viz., धर्म (virtue), अर्थ (wealth), काम (desires of the flesh) and मोक्ष (emancipation). This is generally done through the narration of incidents that took place in the olden days.
The words ‘itihāsa’ and ‘purāṇa’ have often been mentioned in the Vedic literature (vide Atharvaveda 15.6.4; Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 13.4.3.12; Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 2.4.10). There, the difference between the two does not seem to be very clear.
